I reviewed the uncommitted change to `model/features.py` and reported two findings. I didn't run the code or any tests.

1. **Data leakage (confirmed, `model/features.py:14`):** `build_features` standardizes using the mean and standard deviation of the whole dataset. `train.py:15` calls it before the train/test split at line 16, so test rows influence the scaling. The reported AUC will be slightly optimistic. The same code also can't be reused at prediction time, because a new batch would be scaled with its own statistics instead of the training ones. The fix is to fit a `StandardScaler` on the training split only, ideally in a `Pipeline` with `LogisticRegression`, and save it for inference.

2. **NaN or inf from constant columns (plausible, `model/features.py:14`):** A column with zero spread, or a single-row frame, makes the standard deviation 0 or NaN. The standardized column then becomes NaN or inf, and scikit-learn's `LogisticRegression` raises an error on it. I haven't confirmed this on your data.

findings.summary: Standardization uses mean/std computed over the whole DataFrame inside build_features, which runs before train_test_split, so test-set statistics leak into training.
findings.failure_scenario: train.py:15 calls build_features(load(path)) on the full dataset, then splits at line 16. The scaler's mean/std include the test rows, so the reported test AUC is slightly optimistic. At inference time, build_features on a single row or small batch gives NaN (std of 1 row is NaN) or uses different statistics than training, so predictions are inconsistent with the trained model. Fix: fit a scaler on train only (e.g. sklearn StandardScaler in a Pipeline with LogisticRegression) and persist it for inference.

findings.summary: Division by std yields NaN/inf for constant columns, and the standardization is not reusable at serving time.
findings.failure_scenario: If any column in cols is constant in the input (e.g. a batch where support_tickets is all the same value, or a single-row frame), std() is 0 or NaN, so the column becomes NaN/inf and LogisticRegression.fit/predict raises ValueError on NaN input.
